The tests of homogeneity of variance just described are all very sensitive to violations of
the assumption of normally distributed populations. Box examined the effects of departures
from normality on the Bartlett test and developed from it a more robust one. Analysis of
variance is less sensitive to departures from normality than are these tests of homogeneity of
variance, so when non-normality is suspected in the underlying populations, a small signifi-
cance level may be used with the tests of homogeneity of variance.

31.5 Multiple Comparisons
When the ANOVA F test results in the rejection of the null hypothesis that all treatment
means are equal, this does not indicate which mean differs from another. Some pairs of
means may exhibit significant differences, while others may not. One category of procedures
for making multiple comparisons among pairs of treatment means is called post hoc or a pos-
teriori. Such procedures make all possible comparisons between treatment means; if there
are k treatments, there will be k (k – 1)/2 comparisons. We briefly describe two such tests.
The Scheffé test calculates an F statistic for each comparison being performed, and com-
pares each to a single critical value. If X i
